text.autoconfig.spatialhud.title: Spatial HUD
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideO: Use the Render Mode Slider in Setup to choose one of the two presentations. Method 3 is a real flat panel that exists in the game world, so it is seen in perspective as you look around. Method 4 is a 2.5D approximation drawn in the normal screen layer, which only looks like a flat panel. Both show the same purple panel with the selected HUD inside it. If the capture ever fails, the vanilla HUD is shown with a small red square just above the hotbar's top-left corner.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideW: The purple panel and the captured HUD are one flat surface placed in the Minecraft world, client side only. Its position is set by Forward Distance, Vertical Offset and Horizontal Offset. Its tilt around the left-to-right axis is set by Primary Flat-Map Tilt: that value is the look-down angle at which you face the panel square-on. The panel can be seen even when the view is not looking straight down.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideP: The purple four-corner surface is drawn in the normal GUI layer. It approximates a 3D sheet by moving its corners with look pitch, so it is not a real object in the world. Its corners are set in the Purple Polygon Test category.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.enable: Master switch for Spatial HUD. Turning this off in Setup immediately restores the normal vanilla HUD and hides the purple test surface. The separately bindable Toggle Spatial HUD control changes this exact same saved switch.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showPa: Draw the subtle translucent backing behind the selected lower-HUD surface. Method 3 puts this backing into the same private texture as the icons and text, so it receives exactly the same projective or world-space deformation. In Method 4 it is the translucent purple interior of the four-corner quad; the purple border and corner handles always stay visible.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.onlyDu: Keep the spatial presentation out of inventories, chat, pause menus, Mod Menu, and other screens. This is recommended for normal play. Texture methods enforce the same screen-open boundary even if this option is turned off, because they intentionally capture gameplay HUD roots only.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.render: Move this slider to choose the active mode: 3 is the real 3D world-space panel, 4 is the purple 2.5D GUI approximation.
Legacy saved value. Use Render Mode Slider above instead.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.distan: Shared placement distance in block-like units, measured forward from the player-local panel origin. Method 3 is placed by the anchor below. Increasing this makes the panel appear farther away and smaller in perspective; extremely low values are clamped to keep the plane in front of the camera.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.planeW: Physical width of the complete captured panel, including the hotbar and surrounding selected roots. The height is derived from the HUD capture envelope so aspect ratio stays intact. This is a geometric size control shared by Methods 3 and 4, not a separate scale for each HUD element.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Move the panel sideways within its active horizontal anchor. Positive values move right and negative values move left. With Method 3 set to Camera Yaw, right and left follow the view; with Player Body, they follow the body heading instead.

Move the whole panel up or down relative to eye height. Negative values place it at waist height, as if a flat Minecraft map rests in front of you; positive values raise it. This changes position only—use the three rotation controls below to change the surface itself.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.minimu: This old JSON field is no longer used. Spatial HUD now culls only from real physical depth and viewport intersection, never from a configured camera-pitch cutoff.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Primary Flat-Map Tilt — Left ↔ Right Axis

Rotate the surface around its own left-to-right axis. The 85 degree default is almost horizontal, like a Minecraft map laid flat and viewed from above. Lower values create a deliberately steeper paper-like angle. This is a physical surface angle, not a camera-follow setting.
Fine Tilt Offset — Left ↔ Right Axis

Small additional rotation around the same left-to-right axis as Primary Flat-Map Tilt. Positive values push the far/top edge farther away; negative values pull it closer. Leave this at 0 unless fine-tuning the primary tilt, so the two controls do not unintentionally cancel each other.

Rotate the complete flat map around the player-local vertical up axis. Positive values turn its right edge farther forward and its left edge closer; negative values do the opposite. This is not camera yaw: it deliberately angles the surface left or right within the active horizontal anchor.

Rotate around the axis perpendicular to the paper surface. Positive values raise the right edge and lower the left edge; negative values reverse that slope. It is provided for deliberate three-axis adjustment, but 0 keeps text level and is the recommended normal-play value.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.worldS: Applies only to Method 3. Camera Yaw keeps the physical plane in front while looking left or right, as the other panel placements do. Player Body keeps it at body heading instead, so it can remain at the side while the camera looks elsewhere.

Applies only to Method 3. When enabled, the HUD texture uses the world depth buffer, so terrain or a block between the camera and the plane hides it like a physical object. Disable it to retain the world-space position but draw the panel visibly through terrain.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.polygo: Purple test only. Horizontal position of the top-left square handle as a percentage of the GUI width. 0 is the left edge; 100 is the right edge.
Purple test only. Vertical position of the top-left square handle as a percentage of the GUI height. 0 is the top edge; 100 is the bottom edge.
Purple test only. Horizontal position of the top-right square handle as a percentage of the GUI width.
Purple test only. Vertical position of the top-right square handle as a percentage of the GUI height.
Purple test only. Horizontal position of the bottom-right square handle as a percentage of the GUI width.
Purple test only. Vertical position of the bottom-right square handle as a percentage of the GUI height.
Purple test only. Horizontal position of the bottom-left square handle as a percentage of the GUI width.
Purple test only. Vertical position of the bottom-left square handle as a percentage of the GUI height.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHo: Include the hotbar plus the vanilla spectator menu and spectator tooltip in the spatial panel. Disable this if another HUD mod owns the hotbar or if you want Spatial HUD to present only the status information around it.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showBa: Include the main vanilla status-bar roots: armor, health, hunger, and air. The enlarged lower-HUD source surface carries these roots alongside the hotbar, experience, and held-item information. Decorations injected into selected roots are captured with them.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showXp: Include the vanilla experience progress bar, level number, and adjacent information-bar root. Disable it when another mod supplies a replacement experience display or when a cleaner hotbar-only panel is preferred.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showMo: Include the vanilla mount-health root while riding an entity. It has no effect while no mount-health HUD is active.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHe: Include the transient selected-item name above the lower HUD panel. Disable it if a tooltip or inventory mod already provides a preferred held-item label.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.polygo: Purple test only. The purple surface is a physical sheet held in front of you. It stays in place as you turn and as you look up or down, so your head movement changes its perspective the way a real sheet would. Crouching also moves it, because it is anchored to the ground. Tilt is limited to 70 degrees. Turn this off to keep the quad fixed on screen.
